name: Plato
credit: Portrait: Marie-Lan Nguyen — CC BY 2.5 (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Plato (c. 428 – 348 BC) is credited in the Anthology with a number of short epigrams, love poems and epitaphs among them. Their authenticity is doubtful, and Paton's index gives them to Plato without comment.
The epigrams here are those that Paton's first volume ascribes to Plato.

poems.title: Book V, 78
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: My soul was on my lips as I was kissing Agathon. Poor soul! she came hoping to cross over to him.

poems.title: Book V, 79
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: I throw the apple at thee, and thou, if thou lovest me from thy heart, take it and give me of thy maidenhead; but if thy thoughts be what I pray they are not, take it still and reflect how shortlived is beauty.

poems.title: Book V, 80
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: I am an apple; one who loves thee throws me at thee. But consent, Xanthippe; both thou and I decay.

poems.title: Book VI, 1
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: I, Lats, whose haughty beauty made mock of Greece, I who once had a swarm of young lovers at my doors, dedicate my mirror to Aphrodite, since I wish not to look on myself as I am, and cannot look on myself as I once was.

poems.title: Book VI, 43
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Paton marks the attribution with a query.
poems.text: Some traveller, who stilled here his tormenting thirst in the heat, moulded in bronze and dedicated ex voto this servant of the Nymphs, the damp songster who loves the rain, the frog who takes joy in light fountains ; for it guided him to the water, as he wandered, singing opportunely with its amphibious mouth from the damp hollow. Then, not deserting the guiding voice, he found the drink he longed for.

poems.title: Book VII, 99: On Dio
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: The Fates decreed tears for Hecuba and the Trojan women even at the hour of their birth; and after thou, Dio, hadst triumphed in the accomplishment of noble deeds, the gods spilt all thy far-reaching hopes. But thou liest in thy spacious city, honoured by thy countrymen, Dio, who didst madden my soul with love.

poems.title: Book VII, 100: On Aleais and Phaedrus (not an epitaph)
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Now when I said nothing except just that Alexis is fair, he is looked at everywhere and by everyone when he appears. Why, my heart, dost thou point out bones to dogs and have to sorrow for it afterwards? Was it not thus that I lost Phaedrus?

poems.title: Book VII, 256
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Leaving behind the sounding surge of the Aegean we lie on the midmost of the plains of Ecbatana. Farewell, Eretria, once our glorious country; farewell, Athens, the neighbour of Euboea; farewell, dear Sea.

poems.title: Book VII, 259
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: We are Eretrians from Euboea and we lie near Susa, alas how far from our own land.

poems.title: Book VII, 265
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: I am the tomb of a shipwrecked man, and that opposite is the tomb of a husbandman. So death lies in wait for us alike on sea and land.

poems.title: Book VII, 268
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: I whom ye look upon am a shipwrecked man. The sea pitied me, and was ashamed to bare me of my last vesture. It was a man who with fearless hands stripped me, burdening himself with so heavy a crime for so light a gain. Let him put it on and take it with him to Hades, and let Minos see him wearing my old coat.

poems.title: Book VII, 269
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Mariners, may ye be safe on sea and land; but know that this tomb ye are passing is a shipwrecked man’s.

poems.title: Book VII, 669
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Thou lookest on the stars, my Star. Would I were heaven, to look on thee with many eyes.

poems.title: Book VII, 670
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Or old among the living thou didst shine the Star of morn; now shinest thou in death the Star of eve.

poems.title: Book IX, 51
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Time brings everything; length of years can change names, forms, nature, and fortune.

poems.title: Book IX, 506
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Some say the Muses are nine, but how carelessly ! Look at the tenth, Sappho from Lesbos.

poems.title: Book IX, 747
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: The little jasper stone is carved with five cows all looking alive as they feed. Perhaps they would run away, but now the little herd is confined in the golden pen.

poems.title: Book IX, 823
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Let the cliff clothed in greenery of the Dryads keep silence, and the fountains that fall from the rock, and the confused bleating of the ewes newly lambed ; for Pan himself plays on his sweet-toned pipe, running his pliant lips over the joined reeds, and around with their fresh feet they have started the dance, the Nymphs, Hydriads, and Hamadryads.

poems.title: Book IX, 826: On a Satyr standing by a Well and Love Asleep
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: A cunning master wrought me, the Satyr, son of Bacchus, divinely inspiring the monolith with breath. I am the playmate of the Nymphs, and instead of purple wine I now pour forth pleasant water. Guide thy steps here in silence, lest thou disturb the boy lapped in soft sleep.

poems.title: Book XVI, 13
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Sit down by this high-foliaged vocal pine that quivers in the constant western breeze, and beside my plashing stream Pan’s pipe shall bring slumber to thy charmed eyelids.

poems.title: Book XVI, 160: On the Same
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Paphian Cytherea came through the waves to Cnidus, wishing to see her own image, and having viewed it from all sides in its open shrine, she cried, “Where did Praxiteles see me naked?” Praxiteles did not look on forbidden things, but the steel carved the Paphian as Ares would have her.

poems.title: Book XVI, 161: On the Same
poems.author: Plato
poems.text: Neither did Praxiteles nor the chisel work thee, but so thou standest as of old when thou camest to judgment.

poems.title: Book XVI, 210
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: The heading is lost in the scan; Paton’s Index of Authors lists this epigram under Plato.
poems.text: When we entered the deep-shadowed wood we found within it the son of Cytherea, like unto rosy apples. Nor had he the quiver that holds arrows, nor his bent bow, but they were hanging on the leafy trees, and he lay among the rose-blossoms smiling, bound fast by sleep, and above him the tawny bees were sprinkling on his dainty lips honey dripping from the comb.

poems.title: Lovers' Lips (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Kissing Agathon, I had my soul upon my lips; for it rose, poor wretch, as though to cross over.

poems.title: Love and the Stars (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: On the stars thou gazest, my Star; would I were heaven, that I might look on thee with many eyes.

poems.title: To Aphrodite, by Laïs (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I Laïs who laughed exultant over Greece, I who held that swarm of young lovers in my porches, give my mirror to the Paphian; since such as I am I will not see myself, and such as I was I cannot.

poems.title: On the Eretrian Exiles in Persia (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: We who of old left the booming surge of the Aegean lie here in the mid-plain of Ecbatana: fare thou well, renowned Eretria once our country, farewell Athens nigh to Euboea, farewell dear sea.

poems.title: On the Same (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: We are Eretrians of Euboea by blood, but we lie near Susa, alas! how far from our own land.

poems.title: On a Shipwrecked Sailor (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I am the tomb of one shipwrecked; and that opposite me, of a husbandman; for a common Hades lies beneath sea and earth.

poems.title: On the Same (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Well be with you, O mariners, both at sea and on land; but know that you pass by the grave of a shipwrecked man.

poems.title: Aristophanes (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: The Graces, seeking to take a sanctuary that will not fall, found the soul of Aristophanes.

poems.title: On a Sleeping Satyr (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: This Satyr Diodorus engraved not, but laid to rest; your touch will wake him; the silver is asleep.

poems.title: Beneath the Pine (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Sit down by this high-foliaged voiceful pine that rustles her branches beneath the western breezes, and beside my chattering waters Pan's pipe shall bring drowsiness down on thy enchanted eyelids.

poems.title: The Garden of Pan (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Let the shaggy cliff of the Dryads be silent, and the springs welling from the rock, and the many-mingled bleating of the ewes; for Pan himself makes music on his melodious pipe, running his supple lip over the jointed reeds; and around him stand up to dance with glad feet the water-nymphs and the nymphs of the oakwood.

poems.title: Time the Conqueror (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Time carries all things; length of days knows how to change name and shape and nature and fortune.

poems.title: Reversal (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: A man finding gold left a halter; but he who had left the gold, not finding it, knotted the halter he found.

poems.title: The Light of the Dead (Mackail)
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Morning Star that once didst shine among the living, now deceased thou shinest the Evening Star among the dead.

poems.title: A Grave in Persia
poems.author: Plato
poems.text:
Far from our own Ægean shore
  And the surges booming deep,
Here where Ecbatana's great plain
  Lies broad, we exiles sleep.
Farewell, Eretria the renowned,
  Where once we used to dwell;
Farewell, our neighbour Athens;
  Beloved sea, farewell!

poems.title: Starworship
poems.author: Plato
poems.text:
Thou gazest starward, star of mine, whose heaven I fain would be,
That all my myriad starry eyes might only gaze on thee.

poems.title: The Unset Star
poems.author: Plato
poems.text:
Star that didst on the living at dawn thy lustre shed,
Now as the star of evening thou shinest with the dead!

poems.title: Lais
poems.author: Plato
poems.text:
I that through the land of Hellas
  Laughed in triumph and disdain,
Lais, of whose open porches
  All the love-struck youth were fain,
Bring the mirror once I gazed in,
  Cyprian, at thy shrine to vow,
Since I see not there what once was,
  And I would not what is now.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.78: τὴν ψυχήν, Ἀγάθωνα φιλῶν, ἐπὶ χείλεσιν ἔσχον
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
τὴν ψυχήν, Ἀγάθωνα φιλῶν, ἐπὶ χείλεσιν ἔσχον
ἦλθε γὰρ ἡ τλήμων ὡς διαβησομένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.79: τῷ μήλῳ βάλλω σε· σὺ δʼ εἰ μὲν ἑκοῦσα φιλεῖς με,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
τῷ μήλῳ βάλλω σε· σὺ δʼ εἰ μὲν ἑκοῦσα φιλεῖς με,
δεξαμένη, τῆς σῆς παρθενίης μετάδος·
εἰ δʼ ἄρʼ ὃ μὴ γίγνοιτο νοεῖς, τοῦτʼ αὐτὸ λαβοῦσα
σκέψαι τὴν ὥρην ὡς ὀλιγοχρόνιος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.80: μῆλον ἐγώ· βάλλει με φιλῶν σέ τις. ἀλλʼ ἐπίνευσον,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
μῆλον ἐγώ· βάλλει με φιλῶν σέ τις. ἀλλʼ ἐπίνευσον,
Ξανθίππη· κἀγὼ καὶ σὺ μαραινόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.1: ἡ σοβαρὸν γελάσασα καθʼ Ἑλλάδος, ἥ ποτʼ ἐραστῶν
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἡ σοβαρὸν γελάσασα καθʼ Ἑλλάδος, ἥ ποτʼ ἐραστῶν
ἑσμὸν ἐπὶ προθύροις Λαῒς ἔχουσα νέων,
τῇ Παφίῃ τὸ κάτοπτρον· ἐπεὶ τοίη μὲν ὁρᾶσθαι
οὐκ ἐθέλω, οἵη δʼ ἦν πάρος οὐ δύναμαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.43: τὸν Νυμφῶν θεράποντα, φιλόμβριον, ὑγρὸν ἀοιδόν,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
τὸν Νυμφῶν θεράποντα, φιλόμβριον, ὑγρὸν ἀοιδόν,
τὸν λιβάσιν κούφαις τερπόμενον βάτραχον
χαλκῷ μορφώσας τις ὁδοιπόρος εὖχος ἔθηκε,
καύματος ἐχθροτάτην δίψαν ἀκεσσάμενος·
πλαζομένῳ γὰρ ἔδειξεν ὕδωρ, εὔκαιρον ἀείσας
κοιλάδος ἐκ δροσερῆς ἀμφιβίῳ στόματι.
φωνὴν δʼ ἡγήτειραν ὁδοιπόρος οὐκ ἀπολείπων
εὗρε πόσιν γλυκερῶν ὧν ἐπόθει ναμάτων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.99: δάκρυα μὲν Ἑκάβῃ τε καὶ Ἰλιάδεσσι γυναιξὶ
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
δάκρυα μὲν Ἑκάβῃ τε καὶ Ἰλιάδεσσι γυναιξὶ
Μοῖραι ἐπέκλωσαν δή ποτε γεινομέναις·
σοὶ δέ, Δίων, ῥέξαντι καλῶν ἐπινίκον ἔργων
δαίμονες εὐρείας ἐλπίδας ἐξέχεαν·
κεῖσαι δʼ εὐρυχόρῳ ἐν πατρίδι τίμιος ἀστοῖς,
ὦ ἐμὸν ἐκμήνας θυμὸν ἔρωτι Δίων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.100: νῦν ὅτε μηδέν, Ἄλεξις, ὅσον μόνον εἶφʼ, ὅτι καλός,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
νῦν ὅτε μηδέν, Ἄλεξις, ὅσον μόνον εἶφʼ, ὅτι καλός,
ὦπται, καὶ πάντῃ πᾶσι περιβλέπεται.
θυμέ, τί μηνύεις κυσὶν ὀστέον, εἶτʼ ἀνιήσει
ὕστερον; οὐχ οὕτω Φαῖδρον ἀπωλέσαμεν;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.256: οἵδε ποτʼ Αἰγαίοιο βαρύβρομον οἶδμα λιπόντες
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
οἵδε ποτʼ Αἰγαίοιο βαρύβρομον οἶδμα λιπόντες
Ἐκβατάνων πεδίῳ κείμεθʼ ἐνὶ μεσάτῳ.
χαῖρε, κλυτή ποτε πατρὶς Ἐρέτρια· χαίρετʼ, Ἀθῆναι
γείτονες Εὐβοίης· χαῖρε, θάλασσα φίλη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.259: Εὐβοίης γένος ἐσμὲν Ἐρετρικόν, ἄγχι δὲ Σούσων
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
Εὐβοίης γένος ἐσμὲν Ἐρετρικόν, ἄγχι δὲ Σούσων
κείμεθα· φεῦ, γαίης ὅσσον ἀφʼ ἡμετέρης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.265: Ναυηγοῦ τάφος εἰμί ὁ δʼ ἀντίον ἐστὶ γεωργοῦ·
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
Ναυηγοῦ τάφος εἰμί ὁ δʼ ἀντίον ἐστὶ γεωργοῦ·
ὡς ἁλὶ καὶ γαίῃ ξυνὸς ὕπεστʼ Ἀίδης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.268: Ναυηγόν με δέδορκας. ὃν οἰκτείρασα θάλασσα
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
Ναυηγόν με δέδορκας. ὃν οἰκτείρασα θάλασσα
γυμνῶσαι πυμάτου φάρεος ᾐδέσατο,
ἄνθρωπος παλάμῃσιν ἀταρβήτοις μʼ ἀπέδυσε,
τόσσον ἄγος τόσσου κέρδεος ἀράμενος.
κεῖνο καὶ ἐνδύσαιτο, καὶ εἰς Ἀίδαο φέροιτο,
καί μιν ἴδοι Μίνως τοὐμὸν ἔχοντα ῥάκος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.269: πλωτῆρες, σῴζοισθε καὶ εἰν ἁλὶ καὶ κατὰ γαῖαν
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
πλωτῆρες, σῴζοισθε καὶ εἰν ἁλὶ καὶ κατὰ γαῖαν
ἴστε δὲ ναυηγοῦ σῆμα παρερχόμενοι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.669: ἀστέρας εἰσαθρεῖς ἀστήρ ἐμός. εἴθε γενοίμην
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἀστέρας εἰσαθρεῖς ἀστήρ ἐμός. εἴθε γενοίμην
οὐρανός, ὡς πολλοῖς ὄμμασιν εἰς σὲ βλέπω.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.670: ἀστὴρ πρὶν μὲν ἔλαμπες ἐνὶ ζωοῖσιν Ἑῷος·
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἀστὴρ πρὶν μὲν ἔλαμπες ἐνὶ ζωοῖσιν Ἑῷος·
νῦν δὲ θανὼν λάμπεις Ἕσπερος ἐν φθιμένοις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.51: αἰὼν πάντα φέρει· δολιχὸς χρόνος οἶδεν ἀμείβειν
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
αἰὼν πάντα φέρει· δολιχὸς χρόνος οἶδεν ἀμείβειν
οὔνομα καὶ μορφὴν καὶ φύσιν ἠδὲ τύχην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.506: ἐννέα τὰς Μούσας φασίν τινες· ὡς ὀλιγώρως·
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἐννέα τὰς Μούσας φασίν τινες· ὡς ὀλιγώρως·
ἠνίδε καὶ Σαπφὼ Λεσβόθεν ἡ δεκάτη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.747: εἰκόνα πέντε βοῶν μικρὰ λίθος εἶχεν ἴασπις,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
εἰκόνα πέντε βοῶν μικρὰ λίθος εἶχεν ἴασπις,
ὡς ἤδη πάσας ἔμπνοα βοσκομένας.
καὶ τάχα κἂν ἀπέφευγε τὰ βοίδια· νῦν δὲ κρατεῖται
τῇ χρυσῇ μάνδρῃ τὸ βραχὺ βουκόλιον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.823: σιγάτω λάσιον Δρυάδων λέπας, οἳ τʼ ἀπὸ πέτρας
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
σιγάτω λάσιον Δρυάδων λέπας, οἳ τʼ ἀπὸ πέτρας
κρουνοί, καὶ βληχὴ πουλυμιγὴς τοκάδων,
αὐτὸς ἐπεὶ σύριγγι μελίζεται εὐκελάδῳ Πάν,
ὑγρὸν ἱεὶς ζευκτῶν χεῖλος ὑπὲρ καλάμων
αἱ δὲ πέριξ θαλεροῖσι χορὸν ποσὶν ἐστήσαντο
Ὑδριάδες Νύμφαι, Νύμφαι Ἁμαδρυάδες.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.13: Ὑψίκομον παρὰ τάνδε καθίζεο φωνήεσσαν
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
Ὑψίκομον παρὰ τάνδε καθίζεο φωνήεσσαν
φρίσσουσαν πυκινοῖς κῶνον ὑπὸ ζεφύροις,
καί σοι καχλάζουσιν ἐμοῖς παρὰ νάμασι σύριγξ
θελγομένων ἄξει κῶμα κατὰ βλεφάρων,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.160: ἡ Παφίη Κυθέρεια, διʼ οἴδματος ἐς Κνίδον ἦλθε,
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἡ Παφίη Κυθέρεια, διʼ οἴδματος ἐς Κνίδον ἦλθε,
βουλομένη κατιδεῖν εἰκόνα τὴν ἰδίην
πάντῃ δʼ ἀθρήσασα περισκέπτῳ ἐνὶ χώρῳ,
φθέγξατο· ποῦ γυμνὴν εἶδέ με Πραξιτέλης;
Πραξιτέλης οὐκ εἶδεν ἃ μὴ θέμις· ἀλλʼ ὁ σίδηρος
ἔξεσεν οἷʼ ἂν Ἄρης ἤθελε τὴν Παφίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.161: οὔτε σε Πραξιτέλης τεχνάσατο, οὔθʼ ὁ σίδαρος·
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
οὔτε σε Πραξιτέλης τεχνάσατο, οὔθʼ ὁ σίδαρος·
ἀλλʼ οὕτως ἔστης, ὥς ποτε κρινομένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.210: ἄλσος δʼ ὡς ἱκόμεσθα βαθύσκιον, εὕρομεν ἔνδον
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
ἄλσος δʼ ὡς ἱκόμεσθα βαθύσκιον, εὕρομεν ἔνδον
πορφυρέοις μήλοισιν ἐοικότα παῖδα Κυθήρης.
οὐδʼ ἔχεν ἰοδόκον φαρέτρην, οὐ καμπύλα τόξα·
ἀλλὰ τὰ μὲν δένδρεσσιν ὑπʼ εὐπετάλοισι κρέμαντο,
αὐτὸς δʼ ἐν καλύκεσσι ῥόδων πεπεδημένος ὕπνῳ
εὗδεν μειδιόων· ξουθαὶ δʼ ἐφύπερθε μέλισσαι
κηροχύτου μέλιτος ˘ λαροῖς ἐπὶ χείλεσι ῥαῖνον

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.248: τὸν Σάτυρον Διόδωρος ἐκοίμισεν, οὐκ ἐτόρευσεν.
poems.author: Plato
poems.note: Ascribed to Plato in the Greek Anthology.
poems.text:
τὸν Σάτυρον Διόδωρος ἐκοίμισεν, οὐκ ἐτόρευσεν.
ἢν νύξῃς, ἐγερεῖς· ἄργυρος ὕπνον ἔχει.

poems.title: Epigram on Aristophanes: Αἱ Χάριτες τέμενός τι λαβεῖν ὅπερ οὐχὶ πεσεῖται
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology, Greek text (Mackail, 1890)
poems.text:
Αἱ Χάριτες τέμενός τι λαβεῖν ὅπερ οὐχὶ πεσεῖται
ζητοῦσαι ψυχὴν εὗρον Ἀριστοφάνους.

poems.title: Epigram on the Gold and the Halter: Χρυσὸν ἀνὴρ εὑρὼν ἔλιπεν βρόχον
poems.author: Plato
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology, Greek text (Mackail, 1890)
poems.text:
Χρυσὸν ἀνὴρ εὑρὼν ἔλιπεν βρόχον· αὐτὰρ ὁ χρυσὸν
ὃν λίπεν οὐχ εὑρὼν ἦψεν ὃν εὗρε βρόχον.
